correctness.rationale: With x_s=√(a/b), s=at and h=A/(ax_s), the post-reset flow is y′=h+y−y³ and the age has exponential rate ρ=r/a; the chance of no reset in time s is e^{−ρs}, so the age mixture is stationary and unique. For h>0 the positive path increases to the stable root 1+O(h). The tail identity is m=∫₀^{y_+}e^{−ρτ_h(y)}dy. Subtracting log(1+y/h) from the hitting time leaves R_h≥0, with R_h(y)≤y²/[2(1−y²)] for y<1 and fixed-y limit −(1/2)log(1−y²), by domination of the positive remainder integrand. For ρ<1, y^{−ρ} dominates the rescaled integrand, and the interval above 1 contributes O(h)=o(h^ρ); substituting y² in the limiting integral gives the asserted beta coefficient. For ρ>1, y=hv makes (1+v)^{−ρ} an integrable majorant, and R_h(hv)→0, giving 1/(ρ−1). Independently, for λ in a fixed compact set and ρ=1+λ/L, the integral differs from ∫₀¹(1+y/h)^{−ρ}dy by O(h) uniformly: on [0,1/2] the integrand difference is bounded by C y²(1+y/h)^{−ρ}; on the rest each integral has O(h^ρ)=O(h) mass. With t=log(1+y/h)/L the comparison integral divided by hL is ∫₀^{log(1+1/h)/L}e^{−λt}dt, giving local uniformity and the log law at λ=0. Reflection gives oddness, and the susceptibility uses the difference quotient m/h, not differentiation through a divergent integral. This proof replays directly from the scalar hitting-time identity and the stated bounds. The supplied SciPy checks are finite corroboration only and were inspected, not run.

value.rationale: Separates regimes in which differentiating a stationary response through a reset-age average is valid from those where rare long growth intervals dominate. The exact beta amplitude and compact-uniform crossover quantify more than the instability exponent or escape scale; they give a sharp boundary between singular and ordinary static response in a natural model already used for periodic gain. The result does not claim noise robustness or finite-frequency predictions.
